1. Project Overview & Architecture

LPUtility is a web application and native Android WebView application designed for IT and Computer Science students, network technicians, and developers. It provides multi-region network diagnostics, BGP routing intelligence, subnet calculations, and cryptographic utilities in one responsive, high-performance interface.

1.1 Problem Addressed

The initial prototype relied on local PowerShell scripts and third-party package links without real-time telemetry. In this release, LPUtility integrates two complementary live APIs to provide actionable network diagnostics:

  • Multi-Region Latency & Reachability: Testing targets from Europe, Asia, North America, and Oceania using distributed probes.
  • Autonomous System & BGP Context: Identifying the authoritative Autonomous System Number (ASN), organization owner, and BGP prefix block.
  • Offline Protocol Utilities: Interactive IPv4 VLSM subnetting, 128-bit IPv6 RFC 5952 calculations, and NIST SP 800-63B password/key generation.

2. Dual-API Integration

LPUtility integrates two live, production-grade APIs that work together to provide complete network diagnostic information:

API Provider Endpoints Data Provided Access Method
Globalping API jsDelivr POST /v1/measurements
GET /v1/measurements/{id}		 Multi-continent ping, DNS, HTTP, and traceroute latency, packet loss, and jitter. Public REST API, open CORS (*), no client secrets.
RIPE Stat API RIPE NCC GET /data/network-info/
GET /data/as-overview/		 Authoritative ASN, organization holder, BGP prefix, and allocation registry. Public RIR data API, open CORS (*), no API key needed.

2.1 API Synergy

When a diagnostic test is triggered for a target (e.g. 1.1.1.1 or google.com), LPUtility dispatches active probes across multiple continents through Globalping while concurrently querying RIPE Stat for BGP routing information. The user sees active round-trip measurements alongside the network owner and BGP prefix block.

2.2 Code Implementation (from src/services/telemetryAggregator.js)

export async function runCombinedTelemetry({ type = 'ping', target, locations }) {
  // Concurrently dispatch Globalping active probes and RIPE Stat BGP routing lookup
  const globalpingPromise = executeGlobalpingTest({ type, target, locations });
  const ripestatPromise = fetchInfrastructureTelemetry(target);

  const [globalpingResult, ripestatResult] = await Promise.all([
    globalpingPromise.catch(err => null),
    ripestatPromise.catch(err => null)
  ]);

  return { target, type, globalping: globalpingResult, ripestat: ripestatResult };
}

3. Responsive Design & Media Queries

The application adapts cleanly across desktop, tablet, and mobile viewports down to 320px width using clean CSS Flexbox, CSS Grid, and media queries in src/styles/layout.css: 

/* Tablet & Mobile Breakpoint (<= 768px) */
@media (max-width: 768px) {
  .mobile-menu-btn { display: inline-flex; }
  .desktop-toggle-btn { display: none; }
  .winui-sidebar {
    position: fixed; top: 50px; bottom: 0; left: 0;
    width: 240px; transform: translateX(-100%);
    z-index: 150; box-shadow: 4px 0 20px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.7);
  }
  .winui-sidebar.mobile-open { transform: translateX(0); }
  .main-content { padding: 12px 12px 50px 12px; }
  .results-grid { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
}

/* Small Smartphone Viewport (<= 480px) */
@media (max-width: 480px) {
  .target-input-row { flex-direction: column; }
  .run-btn { width: 100%; }
  .summary-card { flex-direction: column; align-items: stretch; }
  .tools-grid { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
}

4. Android Native WebView Implementation

The Android Studio project is located in responsive webview/, built with Kotlin for SDK 35 (Android 15):

  • Back Navigation: Modern OnBackPressedCallback checks webView.canGoBack() to navigate through browser history before exiting.
  • URL Routing: Application routes and local assets stay inside WebView; external links open in the device browser via Intent.ACTION_VIEW.
  • Progress & Refresh: Custom WebChromeClient updates the horizontal progress bar; SwipeRefreshLayout enables pull-to-refresh.
  • Offline Bundle: Bundled web assets at app/src/main/assets/web/ ensure full functionality even when offline.
